# Set-ZbxHttpTest

## SYNOPSIS

Changes a web scenario.

## SYNTAX

```
Set-ZbxHttpTest [-Id] <ulong> [-Name <string>] [-Delay <string>] [-Retries <int>] [-Agent <string>] [-Status <ZabbixHttpTestStatus>] [-Authentication <ZabbixHttpAuthentication>] [-HttpUser <string>] [-HttpPassword <SecureString>] [-Step <ZabbixHttpTestUpdateStepRequest[]>] [-HttpProxy <string>] [-VerifyPeer <bool>] [-VerifyHost <bool>] [-SslCertFile <string>] [-SslKeyFile <string>] [-SslKeyPassword <SecureString>] [-Variable <ZabbixHttpTestVariableRequest[]>] [-Header <ZabbixHttpTestHeaderRequest[]>] [-Tag <ZabbixTagRequest[]>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-PassThru] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Set-ZbxHttpTest cmdlet changes the web scenario in -Id, or a scenario piped from Get-ZbxHttpTest, with httptest.update; a setting whose parameter is not given keeps its value. -Step replaces every step the scenario has. With -PassThru the command reads the scenario back and writes it; without it, it writes nothing. -WhatIf shows what would change.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Check a scenario every five minutes

```powershell
Get-ZbxHttpTest -Name 'Web checkout' | Set-ZbxHttpTest -Delay '5m' -PassThru | Select-Object Name, Delay
```

A scenario piped from Get-ZbxHttpTest binds -Id by its HttpTestId.

### Example 2: Replace a scenario's steps

```powershell
Get-ZbxHttpTest -Name 'Web checkout' | Set-ZbxHttpTest -Step @(
    New-ZbxHttpTestStep 'Home page' 'https://shop.example.com/' -StatusCodes '200'
    New-ZbxHttpTestStep 'Cart' 'https://shop.example.com/cart' -StatusCodes '200'
)
```

-Step replaces the whole list, so give every step the scenario should keep.
